reviews.body:
Thanks for the detailed validation matrix — the engineering here is real and in the right place: it inherits `FlashAttentionBackend`, reuses the parent CP strategy, keeps the code under `hardware_backend/musa/`, and the long comment block at `:468-498` is the most useful thing I read in this diff. I reviewed against the parent (`layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py`) and against the review history for this subsystem. The blocking items are all about **silent staleness** and **silent wrong-side selection** in the graph-replay and CP paths, plus one unvalidated MLA prefill argument mismatch — which is also where this file has already shipped a CP correctness fix (#23270). ### How the change runs ```mermaid flowchart TD A["init_forward_metadata()"] --> A1["super() + _ensure_metadata_types()
parent metadata → Musa* subclasses"] A1 --> A3{"input_ids empty?
(empty DP rank)"} A3 -->|yes| A4["return early, no metadata"] A3 -->|no| B["_init_scheduler_metadata()"] B --> B1{"use_mla?"} B1 -->|yes| B2["_init_mla_scheduler_metadata()"] B1 -->|no| B3["_init_no_mla_scheduler_metadata()"] B2 --> C["_init_cp_scheduler_metadata()"] B3 --> C C --> C1["_cp_side_lengths(): 3× .item() sync"] C2 --> D["_build_scheduler_metadata() → get_scheduler_metadata()"] C --> C2["_init_cp_self / _local / _side"] G["init_forward_metadata_out_graph(in_capture)"] --> G2{"in_capture?"} G2 -->|yes| G3["capture: build + record slots"] G2 -->|no| G4["replay: rebuild + copy into captured tensors"] F["forward_extend / forward_decode"] --> F1["_scheduler_metadata_for_kvcache()
full / swa / encoder / local"] F --> F2["_cp_scheduler_metadata_for_kvcache()
side from tensor identity"] F1 --> H["flash_attn_with_kvcache(scheduler_metadata=…, num_splits=…)"] F2 --> H classDef added fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:2px class A1,B,B2,B3,C,C1,C2,D,G3,G4,F1,F2 added ``` Green = added by this PR. ### Prior art for this subsystem Corpus sweep: **32,639 threads scanned, 405 matched across 142 PRs, 681 human comments** (`hardware_backend/`, `layers/attention/`; terms: cuda graph, scheduler metadata, num_splits, split-kv, context parallel, cross attention, musa). Four opinions bear on this diff: 1. When the MUSA backend moved to inheritance, the ask was to **drop the platform shim** ("I don't know if `FlashAttentionContext` … are still necessary here. Because this time, we choose to inherit from `FlashAttentionBackend`" — #22051). This PR inherits, but then disables a parent hook and rebuilds the lifecycle beside it. 2. **No `seq_lens.max().item()` in the hot path** ("We should avoid CPU-GPU synchronization … Can you derive this value from `seq_lens_cpu`?" — #4514). 3. MUSA-specific code belongs under `hardware_backend/musa/` and aligned with the existing call site (#23270) — honored here. 4. This file already shipped one CP correctness fix ("Resolve output garbage in Context Parallel on MusaFlashAttentionBackend", #23270), so CP paths need correctness evidence, not smoke. ### Additional findings (beyond the inline comments) **P1** - **CP decode synchronizes the device 3× per side, per step.** `_cp_side_lengths()` does `int(q_lens.sum().item())`, `int(k_lens.max().item())`, `int(q_lens.max().item())` (`:820-823`) inside `init_forward_metadata`, i.e. right before every graph replay. Derive `max_seqlen_q`/`max_seqlen_k` from the CP metadata's CPU-side lengths; this is the pattern maintainers have pushed back on before (see corpus item 2). **P2** - **The parent hook is disabled rather than generalized.** `self._get_scheduler_metadata = None` (`:262`) exists because the parent callback uses the FA3 signature (`num_heads`) while MATE needs `num_heads_q` / `num_heads_kv`. A small signature widening in the parent would let both backends share the hook. - **Non-uniform attention layouts become a startup crash.** `_get_no_mla_layer_attention_layouts()` raises `ValueError` when full-attention layers disagree on layout (`:360-374`). A model that the CUDA backend serves becomes unusable on MUSA. Falling back to per-call metadata keeps coverage; if you keep the raise, name the model and the divergent layers in the message. - **The empty-DP-rank early return rests on an unverified claim** (`:1364-1373`). If the attention forward is not actually a shape-preserving no-op, the wrapper's `assert scheduler_metadata is not None` (`:154`) fires. A pointer to the code that guarantees the no-op would make this reviewable. - **`_gather_paged_kv_for_varlen()` materializes the entire prefix KV** (Python loop + `torch.cat`, `:1479-1509`). It is only reachable from the `deterministic_cached_prefix` branch (`:1815`), so it is acceptable — but it is O(prefix) device memory and its `assert seq_lens is not None` (`:1486`) would fire under capture, because `_seq_lens_cpu_list()` returns `None` in capture mode (`:299-300`). A comment stating "eager-only, deterministic path only" would prevent a future caller from wiring it into a graph. **P3** - `assert` used for user-facing preconditions in the wrapper (`:154`) and in the hot path (`:1456`). Prefer `ValueError` / `RuntimeError`. - `seq_lens_sum` and `seq_lens_cpu` are accepted and never used by `_prepare_graph_replay_scheduler_metadata()` (`:1346-1359`). - `_max_seqlen_from_metadata()` still reaches `cache_seqlens.max().item()` on the eager path (`:748`) whenever `max_seq_len_k` is unset. ### CI All three "PR Test" checks are red on the **`run-ci` label gate**, not on code — run 40871271611, step *Require run-ci label (optional)*: `Missing required label 'run-ci'`. That means the new registered CPU suite has **never executed in CI**; please add the label so the 15 tests actually run before this is considered. ### Test gaps The 15 tests are mock-level metadata tests. Nothing covers the graph copy-back path, the CP side selection, `num_splits` agreement between `get_scheduler_metadata()` and the call site, or MLA prefill. Three tests assert the *absence* of methods (`test_removed_legacy_cuda_graph_metadata_hooks`, `test_musa_scheduler_helper_does_not_override_parent_hook`) rather than behavior, so they keep passing even if the replacement logic is wrong. A harness that fakes two captures and one replay and asserts the captured tensors actually changed would cover the riskiest ~60 lines in the PR in ~30 lines of test. ### Verdict Blocking: the inline items (graph-metadata refresh is silent on failure and guarded only by `assert`; the MLA `causal` mismatch; CP side inferred from tensor identity; the hand-maintained slot list; the Gemma4 split policy contradicting itself with no measurement) plus the CP per-step syncs. Requesting changes.
